evidence.description: The supplied date is used in floating-point arithmetic whose result is converted directly to Int without checking finiteness or representable bounds.

candidates.explanation: The public method accepts an arbitrary Date and converts the computed floating-point projection directly to Int. Swift traps when this value is non-finite or outside Int's representable range. There is no validation before the conversion, so an extreme or non-finite date, or sufficiently large statistics values, can cause a runtime failure.
candidates.title: Unchecked floating-point conversion can trap
